text: Initial reading: Q gives an LMI-designed resource-allocation mechanism and mean-square convergence of stochastic proximal best responses; P gives split-conformal, room-level calibration plus a deterministic margin transfer to simultaneous first-gate correctness. I am testing whether P\(\)s calibration-to-interface pattern yields a finite-sample, selective certificate for Q\(\)s realized resource feasibility or equilibrium accuracy, while checking Q\(\)s exact assumptions and dynamics first.

Q studies a deterministic-capacity resource mechanism with stochastic valuation samples (manager problem and payment design), whereas P certifies only a geometric wall-distance gate through a calibrated Hausdorff margin (Proposition 1 and Theorem 1). I will test whether P\(\text{\textquotesingle}\)s room-level marginal interface certificate can yield a meaningful capacity-feasibility or equilibrium guarantee for Q, and record where the required wall-to-capacity or information assumptions fail. I will also audit Q\(\text{\textquotesingle}\)s LMI and convergence claims for a sharper pair-specific obstruction.

Alternative to uncertain capacity: use P\(\text{\textquotesingle}\)s split-conformal score-to-margin pattern to certify a finite iterate of Q\(\text{\textquotesingle}\)s stochastic best-response game. Q P1 asserts strict negativity of the symmetric pseudogradient Jacobian; if this gives strong anti-monotonicity modulus \(m>0\) on compact product strategy set \(S\), then the VI gap \(g(s)=\sup_{z\in S}\langle F(s),z-s\rangle\) bounds \(m\|s-s^*\|^2\). With sampled gradient \(\widehat F\) and error \(e=\|F(s)-\widehat F(s)\|\), \(g(s)\leq\widehat g(s)+\operatorname{diam}(S)e\). A P-style episode-level conformal radius for \(e\) would thus give a marginal finite-time bound on distance to Q\(\text{\textquotesingle}\)s unique NE. I am checking calibration observability, adaptivity, and strategic reporting before claiming this as a result.

Q, Proposition 2 (lines 410–427) claims its explicit payment (40) satisfies P1, while P1 (lines 200–211) requires \(\Psi+\Psi^\top\preceq-\upsilon I\) for \(\upsilon>0\). Direct differentiation of (40) for scalar resources and quadratic \(V_n(x_n)=b_nx_n-\alpha x_n^2/2\) gives the negative utility pseudogradient \(F_{x_n}=-V_n^{\prime}(x_n)+\alpha[-p_n/(N-1)+N\bar p_{-n}/(N-1)^2]\), \(F_{p_n}=\alpha[p_n-\bar p_{-n}/(N-1)-(\sum_m x_m-c)/(N-1)]\). On the consensus direction \(\Delta x_n=a,\Delta p_n=b\) for every agent, \(\Delta s^\top(DF+DF^\top)\Delta s/2=N\alpha[a^2-ab/(N-1)]\), negative at \(a=b/[2(N-1)]\). Thus the explicit payment cannot satisfy the claimed strong-monotonicity LMI for any \(N\ge2\). I am checking whether this is an indexing/calculation error and what it means for the Q–P combination.

Stronger, payment-independent obstruction: Q P2(i), Theorem 1 (lines 240–250), requires \(\sum_m A_{nm}^n=0\) for every \(n\). Since \(\partial^2 U_n/\partial p_n\partial p_m=-A_{nm}^n\), the full utility pseudogradient Jacobian \(J\) has zero quadratic form on every nonzero uniform-price direction \(v=(\Delta x_n=0,\Delta p_n=q)_{n=1}^N\): \(v^\top Jv=-\sum_n q^\top(\sum_m A_{nm}^n)q=0\). Q P1(ii), Proposition 1 (lines 200–211), requires \(v^\top(J+J^\top)v\le-\upsilon\|v\|^2<0\), impossible. The same argument applies directly to Q\(\text{\textquotesingle}\)s \(\Psi\) because its price-price blocks are \(-A_{nm}^n\). So Q\(\text{\textquotesingle}\)s P1 and P2 LMIs have empty intersection for \(N\ge2\), including the claimed witness (40), independent of valuation curvature. This blocks Ada\(\text{\textquotesingle}\)s proposed global strong-monotonicity modulus for the Q-specific mechanism; one may seek a weaker residual bound or price normalization instead.

A direct check breaks the strong-monotonicity premise of my proposed VI-gap certificate for Q\(\text{\textquotesingle}\)s explicit payment (Q Eq. (40)). Differentiating its own-price terms gives \(F_{p_n}=\alpha[-p_n+\frac{1}{N-1}\sum_{m\ne n}p_m+\frac{1}{N-1}(\sum_m x_m-c)]\). For the nonzero direction \(v=(0_x,q,\ldots,q)_p\), \(v^\top(J+J^\top)v=0\): common price shifts leave all price gradients unchanged. Thus Q P1(ii), \(\Psi+\Psi^\top\preceq-\upsilon I\) with \(\upsilon>0\), cannot hold for Eq. (40), despite Proposition 2 saying it does. The sharper uniform \((x,p)\) block also has a positive symmetric-Jacobian eigenvalue. Consequently the simple gap bound \(m\|s-s^*\|^2\leq g(s)\) does not follow for the advertised mechanism; a different error-bound argument would be required before P-style calibration transfers to equilibrium accuracy.

Independent check of Q\(\text{\textquotesingle}\)s empirical support: Theorem 4 specifies \(Q_i=\lceil C_b/\eta^{2(i+1)}\rceil\) with \(0<\eta<1\), so samples per iteration grow geometrically. The numerical section instead says \(Q_i=\lceil\widetilde\eta^{i+1}\rceil\) with \(\widetilde\eta=0.96\) (also \(0.97,0.98\)); this equals \(1\) at every iteration. Thus the displayed runs do not instantiate the theorem\(\text{\textquotesingle}\)s vanishing sampling error. A P-style finite-sample certificate would be especially pertinent, but neither source supplies calibration episodes or an exact-gradient/optimum oracle for Q; the simulation cannot serve as such a certificate.

Revised bridge that avoids Q P1: certify Q\(\text{\textquotesingle}\)s planner objective directly at a finite, *feasible* allocation. For any \(\lambda\ge0\), define the Lagrangian duality gap \(G(x,\lambda)=\lambda^\top c+\sum_n\sup_{z_n\in X_n}\{V_n(z_n)-\lambda^\top z_n\}-\sum_n V_n(x_n)\). Q\(\text{\textquotesingle}\)s \(\alpha\)-strong concavity gives \(0\le W(x^o)-W(x)\le G\) and \(\|x-x^o\|^2\le2G/\alpha\) whenever \(x\in X\) and \(\sum_n x_n\le c\). Let \(\widehat G\) use Q\(\text{\textquotesingle}\)s sampled valuations and choose \(\lambda\) from the current price messages. P\(\text{\textquotesingle}\)s episode-level split-conformal pattern applied to the scalar score \((G-\widehat G)_+\) would give a marginal upper radius \(\varepsilon_\alpha\) and hence \(W(x^o)-W(x)\le\widehat G+\varepsilon_\alpha\), \(\|x-x^o\|\le\sqrt{2(\widehat G+\varepsilon_\alpha)/\alpha}\), with abstention on infeasible/large-gap runs. This requires oracle values on calibration episodes and trusted valuation samples; it does not repair Q\(\text{\textquotesingle}\)s P1/P2 inconsistency or certify strategic truthfulness. I will check the exact derivation and whether this is materially more than generic calibration.

Prior-work check narrows the dual-gap idea: search queries `conformal prediction duality gap optimization solution certificate approximate optimality`, `conformal prediction primal dual gap stochastic optimization certificate`, and `conformal prediction equilibrium gap games certificate` found Li et al., *Tightening optimality gap with confidence through conformal prediction*, arXiv:2503.04071, https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.04071. Its abstract explicitly combines conformal prediction with certified primal/dual optimization bounds, so calibrating Q\(\text{\textquotesingle}\)s dual gap is not novel at that generic level. Search also found Fabiani and Franci, *Certifying ε-equilibria in stochastic games with limited data availability*, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejcon.2026.101558, which advertises distribution-free finite-data equilibrium distance certificates. Any publication claim needs Q-specific strategic audit design, an explicit feasible corrected mechanism, or a demonstrable theorem beyond those patterns.

Q P5 has a separate validation gap. Its Assumption 5 simply posits that the proximal best-response map \(T\) is nonexpansive, while the numerical section uses \(\mu=1\) without checking it. For the interior scalar \(N=2\), quadratic \(V_n(x_n)=b_nx_n-\alpha x_n^2/2\), and Q Eq. (40), differentiating the unconstrained \(T\) at an interior point with \(\alpha=\mu=1\) gives operator norm approximately \(1.499>1\) and spectral radius approximately \(1.155>1\). Thus this admissible local configuration violates the theorem\(\text{\textquotesingle}\)s nonexpansiveness hypothesis, independently of the P1/P2 contradiction. I have not yet proved failure for Q\(\text{\textquotesingle}\)s particular 50-agent numerical instance; this is a counterexample to treating the hypothesis as automatic.

Cross-check of Ada entries 8–9: the feasible primal-dual gap inequality is valid under Q\(\text{\textquotesingle}\)s strong concavity, but it needs trusted valuation oracles and finite-iterate feasibility; Q does not provide those. External prior work is real: Li et al., https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.04071, explicitly use conformal prediction to tighten primal/dual optimality bounds; Fabiani and Franci, https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0947358026001111, explicitly give distribution-free finite-data distance certificates for stochastic game equilibria. Generic conformal gap calibration is therefore insufficient as a novelty claim. My P1–P2 incompatibility proof is in emmy/pair_note.md; it applies to the whole Q LMI family, not only payment (40). The most defensible outcome may be a Q correction note, with P motivating a later finite-iteration validation program rather than already yielding a pair-specific publication.

Further Q audit: the Section 4 reduced payment \(\widehat t_n=\alpha[s_n^\top M s_n+(\Delta\bar s_{-n}+d)^\top s_n]\) is not Eq. (40) with opponent-only terms removed. Eq. (40) has own term \(+\alpha p_n^\top p_n/2\), but printed \(M=-\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\ I/(N-1)&I/2\end{pmatrix}\) gives \(-\alpha p_n^\top p_n/2\). Eq. (40) gives coefficients \(+\alpha N\bar p_{-n}^\top x_n/(N-1)^2\) and \(-\alpha p_n^\top\bar x_{-n}/(N-1)\), while printed \(\Delta=-\frac{1}{N-1}\begin{pmatrix}0&I\\-NI/(N-1)&I\end{pmatrix}\) gives \(-\alpha\bar p_{-n}^\top x_n/(N-1)\) and \(+\alpha N p_n^\top\bar x_{-n}/(N-1)^2\). Hence the VS-PBR algorithm as printed solves a different game, so its convergence theorem cannot establish dynamic stability of the explicit Eq. (40) mechanism without correcting the matrices and rechecking Assumption 5.

Final assessment from my side: Q P1(ii) and P2(i) are algebraically incompatible on the common-price direction (proof in emmy/pair_note.md, using Q Proposition 1 and Theorem 1). P Proposition 1/Theorem 1 shows how a calibrated error radius can certify a single downstream interface, but a direct transfer to Q requires a verified efficient reference, whole-game exchangeable calibration episodes, and small finite-iterate errors; Q supplies none, and existing conformal optimality/equilibrium papers cover the generic pattern (URLs in entry 11). I therefore see a potentially publishable Q correction/no-go note, not yet a supported novel joint Q–P result. An unresolved route is a corrected mechanism or dual-gap certificate with auditable valuation data and empirical nonvacuity.

Independent check of Ada entry 12 against Q lines 410–427 and 429–444: Eq. (40) has \(+\alpha p_n^\top p_n/2\), while the displayed reduced \(M\) gives \(-\alpha p_n^\top p_n/2\). The displayed \(\Delta\) also swaps/sign-changes the cross coefficients of \(x_n^\top\bar p_{-n}\) and \(p_n^\top\bar x_{-n}\). These are own-strategy terms, so the claimed elimination of opponent-only terms cannot explain them. Thus the printed Section 4 VS-PBR map is not the best response for Eq. (40). This reinforces that Q\(\text{\textquotesingle}\)s finite-iteration behavior cannot be certified from its current theorem; it does not by itself create a Q–P result.

Cross-checked Emmy\(\text{\textquotesingle}\)s `emmy/pair_note.md`: its P1/P2 zero-price-direction proof is correct and stronger than my Eq. (40)-specific check. A one-line check makes my separate Q payment-reduction mismatch indisputable: take scalar \(N=2\), \(x_1=x_2=0\), \(c=0\), \(p_1=1\), \(p_2=0\), \(\alpha=1\). Q Eq. (40) gives \(t_1=+1/2\); the displayed \(M,\Delta,d\) in the Stochastic Dynamic Stability section give \(\widehat t_1=-1/2\), with all opponent-only terms zero. Thus printed Algorithm 1 optimizes a different own-price payoff at this profile. This obstruction is distinct from the empty P1/P2 LMI intersection.

I wrote the paired derivation and limits in `ada/pair_note.md` (Q source lines and P source lines cited there). The conditional positive result is a feasible-allocation duality-gap certificate: Q\(\text{\textquotesingle}\)s strong concavity converts a calibrated one-sided gap error into marginal welfare and allocation-distance bounds at a fixed finite iterate. It needs trusted exact-gap labels on exchangeable calibration episodes and gives no conditional guarantee among accepted runs. Li et al. (https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.04071) and Fabiani–Franci (https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejcon.2026.101558) make this generic pattern insufficient for a novelty claim. The strongest supported publishable lead from these inputs is the Q P1/P2 no-go correction, supplemented by the independent Eq. (40)/reduced-payment mismatch; P motivates but does not establish a repaired joint mechanism.

Cross-check of Ada entry 16: the scalar profile \(N=2\), \(x_1=x_2=c=0\), \(p_1=1\), \(p_2=0\), \(\alpha=1\) gives \(t_1=1/2\) in Q Eq. (40) (lines 412-418) but \(\widehat t_1=-1/2\) from the displayed \(M,\Delta,d\) (lines 432-440). Since the difference is an own-price term, Q Section 4 cannot follow by dropping opponent-only terms; Algorithm 1 is for a different payoff. I added this check to emmy/pair_note.md. It compounds the P1-P2 LMI incompatibility but does not yield a joint Q-P theorem; P offers a validation pattern only after a corrected game and labelled calibration episodes exist.
